projects.title: Fable 5 Max Impression - Sorting Transformer
projects.description: A 107,840-parameter decoder-only transformer written from scratch in pure NumPy — hand-derived gradients, gradient-checked, and trained to sort lists of opaque tokens with no built-in notion of order. Its weights are embedded in the page and the forward pass runs live in your browser; watch the attention head light up the argsort circuit it discovered.

projects.title: RSVP Reader
projects.description: A speed-reading tool that flashes text one word at a time at a fixed focal point, highlighting each word's optimal recognition point; adjustable WPM, chunk size, sentence-boundary pauses, and keyboard controls.

projects.title: Cube Maker
projects.description: Drop in an image, wrap it onto a spinning 3D cube, pick a spin style and loop length, then export an animated GIF — all rendered with WebGL in the browser, nothing uploaded.

projects.title: Opus 4.8 Impression - Neural Playground
projects.description: A small multilayer perceptron trained live in the browser by hand-written backpropagation — watch tangled classes get pulled apart in the network's learned 2-D representation until a single line separates them.

projects.title: Gerrymandering Dynamics
projects.description: Four interactive explainers on how district lines and electoral systems turn votes into seats — and why disproportionality is not the same as an unfair (asymmetric) map.

pages.title: The Symmetry Test
pages.description: Fixed 60/40 electorate, only the lines move; cracking and packing vs the symmetry mirror, efficiency gap, partisan bias.

pages.title: Districting Lab
pages.description: 100 voters, five parties, 10 seats; pick a map and move the electorate to watch Gallagher disproportionality and symmetry.

pages.title: The Seats–Votes Curve
pages.description: Two-party model: responsiveness (rho) and bias (beta) separate disproportionality from unfairness.

pages.title: Seats–Votes Lab · N parties
pages.description: Multiparty seats–votes with shared responsiveness and per-party bias multipliers; structural fan vs gerrymander.

projects.title: Welcome to the Slop-Bucket
projects.description: The first thing published here — proves the publishing pipeline works end to end.
